arms.name: random_ema
arms.purpose: conservative allocation control receives one additional step and greater cost

motivation: scale-2 harmed low_max_abs relative to random in the scaled-50% experiment; this shot removes only that correction while preserving the priced steps, batch size, backward activity, EMA, and evaluation

execution.sparse_arms: dense forward with gathered 50% FFN backward and no gradient scaling
execution.dense_reference: unchanged ordinary dense training with final 0.95 EMA
execution.deployment: ordinary dense inference with averaged weights

cost_accounting.training: same realized-row CPU-calibrated formula and step pricing as the scaled-50% protocol
cost_accounting.removed_overhead: no gradient-scale multiplications; scoring, gather/scatter and EMA costs remain

primary_endpoint: final EMA ordinary dense held-out loss at training-plus-EMA cost

decision_rules.allocation_failure: unscaled low_max_abs does not beat unscaled random despite random receiving more steps and cost; stop
decision_rules.no_level_3: unscaled low_max_abs beats random but not the unchanged dense EMA reference; stop
decision_rules.development_level_3: unscaled low_max_abs EMA loss is below random and dense EMA while total cost is no greater than either
decision_rules.confirmation: only development_level_3 launches the identical body-7 comparison

prohibited: changing steps, activity, batch size, EMA decay, or evaluation after launch
adding gradient scaling back into either sparse arm
launching body 7 without a development-level win
